indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: Describe the position of objects in space using the cardinal points
indicator.objective: Tell the position and motion of objects in space using the cardinal points north-east, north-west, south-east and south-west

skills.description: State the direction of one point from another using half-cardinal points.
Give step directions on a grid.
Compare two positions using half-cardinal points.

misconceptions: Starting directions from the wrong point
Omitting the half-cardinal point when needed

questions.stem: Point P is above and to the right of point Q on a grid. What is the direction of P from Q?
questions.misconception: Choosing north-west (above and left).

questions.stem: Point A is below and to the left of point B. What is the direction of A from B?
questions.misconception: Choosing south-east (below and right).

questions.stem: On a grid, the church is 3 squares north and 2 squares east of Kofi's house. What is the direction of the church from Kofi's house?
questions.explanation: 3 squares north and 2 squares east means north-east.
questions.misconception: Choosing north-west because both start with 'north'.

questions.stem: The hospital is west of the school. What direction is the school from the hospital?
hints: If A is west of B, then B is east of A.
questions.explanation: The school is east of the hospital.
questions.misconception: Saying west because the hospital was west of the school.

questions.stem: Point X is 4 squares south and 4 squares west of point Y. What is the direction of X from Y?
questions.misconception: Choosing south-east.

questions.stem: From Kofi's house, the market is 2 squares north and 3 squares east. The school is 2 squares north and 3 squares west. What is the direction of the school from the market?
hints: Both are north of Kofi's house.
The market is east; the school is west.
questions.explanation: The school is west of the market.
questions.misconception: Saying east because the market was east of Kofi's house.

questions.stem: Point P is north-west of point Q. Point R is south-east of point Q. What is the direction of P from R?
questions.explanation: From R (down-right), P is up-left relative to Q, so P is north-west of R.
questions.misconception: Saying south-east because R is south-east of Q.

questions.stem: A point A is 5 squares north and 3 squares east of B. A point C is 2 squares south and 1 square west of B. What is the direction of A from C?
hints: C is down-left from B, so A is even further up-right from C.
questions.misconception: Choosing north-west.

questions.stem: Start at point O. Move 2 squares north and 1 square east. What is your new position?
questions.explanation: You end at 2 north and 1 east.
questions.misconception: Swapping north and east.

questions.stem: Start at point (3, 3). Move 2 squares south-west. What is your new position?
hints: South-west means subtract from both coordinates.
questions.misconception: Adding 2 to both coordinates to get (5,5).

questions.stem: From (1, 2), move 3 squares north-east. Where do you end up?
questions.misconception: Subtracting 3 from y instead of adding.

questions.stem: A pupil walks from (0, 0) to (3, 4). In which general direction did the pupil move?
hints: From (0,0) to (3,4): x increases, y increases.
questions.explanation: Both coordinates increase, so the direction is north-east.
questions.misconception: Choosing north-west because it starts with north.

questions.stem: From (4, 4), move 3 squares south and 2 squares west. What is the new position?
questions.misconception: Adding 3 and 2.

questions.stem: A boy starts at (2, 2). He walks 2 squares north, then 3 squares east, then 1 square south. Where does he end up?
hints: Track the x and y changes.
questions.misconception: Forgetting the south move and getting (5, 4).

questions.stem: If point A is north-west of point B, then point B is ___ of point A.
questions.explanation: The reverse of north-west is south-east.
questions.misconception: Saying north-west again.

questions.stem: Point T is south-west of point U. Point V is north-east of point U. What is the direction of V from T?
hints: V is up-right of U, so V is even further up-right from T.
questions.misconception: Saying south-west because T was south-west.

questions.stem: Point A is east of point B. Point C is north of point B. What is the direction of A from C?
hints: C is above B, so from C, A is down-right.
questions.misconception: Saying north-east because A is east.

questions.stem: Point P is 2 squares north and 2 squares west of Q. Point R is 2 squares south and 2 squares east of Q. What is the direction of P from R?
questions.explanation: From R, P is up-left, so north-west.
questions.misconception: Saying south-east because R is south-east of Q.

questions.stem: From the market, the school is north-west. From the market, the hospital is south-east. What is the direction of the hospital from the school?
hints: Hospital is down-right, so hospital is even further down-right from school.
questions.explanation: Hospital is south-east of the school.
questions.misconception: Saying south-west.

questions.stem: Point A is 3 squares north-east of point B. Point C is 1 square south-west of point B. What is the direction of A from C?
hints: C is down-left of B, so A is even further up-right from C.
questions.misconception: Saying north-west because A is north-east of B but C is south-west of B.
